subject: Media Literacy
title: Live Video Manipulation
description: A 60-second lesson on Live Video Manipulation.

hook.text: A news channel splits its screen during a protest. The left shows flames. The right shows calm. Same event, two cameras.

buildup.text: Live broadcasts seem uneditable — but camera positioning, split screens, and timing create real-time bias.

discovery.text: Directors choose which camera feed to show. In a crowd, one angle shows chaos; another shows calm.

twist.text: 'Live' coverage creates an illusion of objectivity. But every moment shown is a choice about what not to show.

climax.text: Live doesn't mean unbiased. The camera operator and director are still making editorial decisions in real time.

punchline.text: Live is still edited. The director just edits in real time.

quiz.question: How can live broadcasts be manipulated?
options: They can't — live is always objective
Through camera positioning, angle selection, and split-screen choices
